findings.title: Unauthenticated access to admin APIs and private data
findings.evidence: requiresAdmin() (src/lib/apiAuthorization.ts:4-28) enumerates public methods explicitly and defaults every non-read API method to admin-only (line 27). /api/admin/*, /api/cms, /api/upload, /api/convert-image, /api/ai-jobs are always admin; GET/HEAD on /api/inquiries, list-style /api/orders, and includeDrafts=1 / all=true params require admin. middleware (src/middleware.ts:102-107) enforces this before routing; matcher (lines 238-243) covers /api/:path* and all non-asset pages. Routes also double-check with isAdminRequest where it matters (orders GET line 57, products GET line 91, settings GET/POST). Settings route additionally filters secret keys (isSecretKey regex, src/app/api/settings/route.ts:39) and sanitizes site_settings to a public key whitelist for anonymous callers.
findings.verification: Read all listed files; traced each allowlist branch; confirmed 401 paths are covered for inquiries list, orders list, drafts, storage and diagnostics. Ran tests/scripts/security-regressions.cjs: 18/18 pass on Node v24.19.0, including anonymous/forged/valid admin session cases.
findings.residualRisk: Most routes (inquiries GET/PATCH, orders PATCH, blogs/products write) rely solely on middleware for authorization and perform no in-route check. If a route were ever invoked in a context where middleware does not run (e.g. direct Node dev-server import, future deployment target without middleware support), it would be unauthenticated. Low likelihood on the current Cloudflare Pages + next-on-pages stack. In-memory rate limiter keyed by IP is per-isolate and spoofable via x-forwarded-for when not behind Cloudflare (dev only) - pre-existing, documented as acceptable.

findings.title: Stored HTML / JSON-LD XSS in blog and editor content
findings.evidence: Single shared FilterXSS instance (src/lib/sanitizeHtml.ts) with js-xss default whitelist plus class, iframe restricted to https youtube.com/youtube-nocookie.com /embed/ URLs via onTagAttr (non-absolute or non-embed iframes stripped), and script/style/svg/math/object/template bodies stripped. Applied at write time (blogs POST line 91) and at every render/insertion point: BlogPostClient.tsx:147 (sanitize after normalizeBlogContent, before dangerouslySetInnerHTML at line 179), RichTextEditor init (lines 20, 32), onChange (line 40) and onPaste (line 112); createLink rejects non http/https/mailto/tel schemes (line 60). All raw JSON-LD renderers under src/app escape '<' as \u003c (verified by grep across ~30 sites, e.g. src/app/page.tsx:79, src/components/FaqSection.tsx:22); feeds/supplies.xml escapes to <.
findings.verification: Code review of sanitizer config and all four call sites; grep confirmed every dangerouslySetInnerHTML JSON-LD site carries the .replace(/</g, '\\u003c') guard. Regression suite 18/18 pass includes a real headless-Chrome stored-payload test.
findings.residualRisk: The blogs.schema_jsonld column is stored raw (blogs POST line 102) and is not sanitized; no current code path renders it into a page (verified by grep), so it is inert today, but any future renderer must escape it. Defense in depth only.

findings.title: Payment transaction replay against unrelated orders
findings.evidence: payments/create requires order-scoped receipt cookie or admin (line 25), requires status='pending' (line 31), and persists payment_provider/payment_ref with a conditional UPDATE (status='pending' AND COALESCE(payment_ref,'')=old) before returning the gateway redirect (lines 54-61). payments/callback only accepts orders in pending/paid/processing/dispatched/delivered (cancelled excluded, line 48) and verifies stored provider+transaction reference, merchant ref, exact amount, AED currency, paid/complete state, and PayTabs Sale transaction type (payments.ts:122-131, 172-185). The pending->paid transition is a conditional UPDATE (callback lines 56-65) so replays or races cannot revert dispatched/delivered orders or revive cancelled ones. Anonymous receipt lookup requires an HMAC-signed, 7-day, HttpOnly, Secure-on-HTTPS, SameSite=Lax cookie bound to the specific order ref (orderAccess.ts); refs are generated with crypto.randomUUID; a bare transaction ID grants nothing.
findings.verification: Read all four files end to end; traced create->persist->callback->conditional update flow; confirmed create route rate-limited (30/min) and admin/cookie gated in both middleware and route. Regression tests 18/18 pass including Stripe/PayTabs mismatch, callback replay and cancellation-race cases.
findings.residualRisk: Pre-fix in-flight gateway sessions have no persisted payment_ref and will fail closed on callback - documented reconciliation item, requires deployment-transition handling. create route's catch-all returns {online:false} on any internal error, silently masking gateway misconfiguration (customer can still check out; order stays pending). Stripe success callback is a GET with parameters in the URL, so the session_id appears in access logs of whatever proxies handle the return - mitigated because replay of the URL alone cannot flip a non-pending order and grants no receipt access without the cookie.

findings.title: Caller-controlled inquiry IDs enabling lead overwrite/replacement
findings.evidence: Both creation paths generate ids server-side with crypto.randomUUID() and use plain INSERT (inquiries/route.ts:49-63, send-email/route.ts:59-77). No caller-supplied id is accepted anywhere; PATCH (admin-only per middleware) is the only mutation path.
findings.verification: Read both routes; confirmed no UPSERT/REPLACE on inquiries.
findings.residualRisk: Inquiry POST performs no field validation (empty name/email accepted). Spam-only impact; mitigated by the 10/min/IP middleware tier.

findings.title: Quote/email endpoint: recipient injection, unbounded input, fire-and-forget persistence
findings.evidence: Zod schema strips unknown fields including any visitor-supplied recipient (quote-input.ts); route requires application/json, caps body at 16 KiB, enforces honeypot (website field), pins notificationEmail='' so the server resolves smtp_to_email/notification_email from D1 settings (email-service.ts:369, 124-130). D1 persistence is awaited before responding; 503 only when both delivery and persistence fail. All interpolated HTML fields pass through escapeHtml.
findings.verification: Read all three files; confirmed recipient pinning path and that no visitor field reaches a mail 'to'. The 7 dedicated send-email regression tests (delivery, fallback, 503, awaited persistence, malformed/oversized/honeypot, recipient override) all pass.
findings.residualRisk: None identified beyond the shared rate-limiter caveats.

findings.title: Draft/inactive products and blogs visible to anonymous callers
findings.evidence: products GET appends AND is_active=1 for non-admins on both id and list lookups (route.ts:91-98). blogs GET filters isActive=1 for slug and list, and includeDrafts/id-with-drafts paths are admin-gated both in-route and by middleware's includeDrafts=1 rule (apiAuthorization.ts:25).
findings.verification: Read both routes; traced both lookup branches; middleware param gate confirmed.

findings.title: Non-constant-time signature comparison in admin session verification
findings.evidence: isAdminRequest compares the client-supplied signature to the expected SHA-256 hex with plain string equality (adminAuth.ts:49) rather than a constant-time comparison, unlike the login route which deliberately compares both credentials before failing.
findings.residualRisk: Theoretical timing side-channel on hex-digit prefix matching across a network to a Cloudflare edge worker; exploiting it to forge a session is impractical. Worth fixing with a constant-time compare when touching the file.

findings.title: Internal error details reflected in public API responses
findings.evidence: Catch blocks return details: String(error) to the caller (e.g. orders POST line 191, PATCH line 212). The public order-creation path can therefore reflect raw D1/driver exception text.
findings.residualRisk: Low-sensitivity schema/driver error text only; no credentials are interpolated. Remove 'details' from public routes for hygiene.

findings.title: Deployment-transition and environment validation still open
findings.evidence: Fixes are validated locally (regression suite 18/18 on Node v24.19.0, re-run during this review) but not against production Cloudflare middleware execution, real hosted-payment cookie persistence, real gateway responses, or the pre-fix in-flight session reconciliation. Production D1 read-only checks were not possible (OAuth token fails D1 API calls, code 10000).
findings.verification: Re-ran node --test tests/scripts/security-regressions.cjs: 18 pass / 0 fail. No live traffic exercised.
findings.residualRisk: All three HIGH fixes depend on middleware running at the edge and ADMIN_PASSWORD being set; validate on a preview deployment before enabling production payment traffic, as the original report states.
